applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and gives as its reason what a single verse, Matthew 1:16, does or does not settle.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: 'ground for' UNDERDETERMINED: whether the clause after the colon is the ground, or the later mention of the rounds' answers is. I read the ambiguity of the single verse as the stated ground, and the round references as a description of what each side said.
why: The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on Matthew 1:16 alone supporting neither reading, which is the single-verse non-statement ground the rule forbids, and it does not weigh the chain of links.
